intent: When any player drops a bomb, a ring spreads out from it and fades, so everyone (players and spectators) sees the danger zone before the blast knocks players out.
accept: Every lit bomb shows a ring centred on it whose radius grows from 0 to 3 tiles over its first 2 seconds
The ring fades out as it expands and is gone after 2 seconds, with no ring left once the bomb has exploded
The ring is visible in the before/after clip for bombs of any player and does not hide players

criteria.text: Every lit bomb shows a ring centred on it whose radius grows from 0 to 3 tiles over its first 2 seconds
criteria.evidence: after/shot-1 and shot-3: orange rings centred on freshly dropped bombs at different growth stages; assets.ts drawBomb uses age 0..30 ticks (2s at 15Hz) and R = t*3*cell.

criteria.text: The ring fades out as it expands and is gone after 2 seconds, with no ring left once the bomb has exploded
criteria.evidence: alpha = 1 - t in assets.ts; the ring is only drawn for age <= 30 of the 45-tick fuse, and older bombs in after/shot-2 and shot-3 have no ring.

criteria.text: The ring is visible in the before/after clip for bombs of any player and does not hide players
criteria.evidence: after/shot-2: ring around the new bomb where before/shot-2 has none; after/shot-3 shows three rings on bombs of different players; the ring is a thin stroke with a 12% fill, and players and labels stay readable.

findings: Optional polish: the ring is circular but real blasts are cross-shaped, so it can overstate danger diagonally. In assets.ts drawBomb, consider clipping or marking the lanes. No test was added, but the change is visual only.
